detections.name: Barnard's Star
detections.note: Measured from these images, Barnard's Star drifts 10.27″ a year. The star catalogue gives 10.39″ a year. The two differ because the measurement also picks up parallax (Earth's own orbit) and some error in finding the star's centre.

notes: It moves across the sky faster than any other star, 10.4″ a year, almost due north.
This object is so bright that the centre of its image is saturated in 24 of 24 frames. Its brightness values here are not reliable; they show as hollow points in the charts.
The crosshair shows where the star catalogue says the object should be on each date, given its motion of 10.4″ a year. Across these frames that is a shift of 1.9 pixels (11.5″).
